baseline_prompt_en: At dawn after a storm, one original adult fictional woman serving as a maritime police or coast guard officer works on the wet deck of a marked coastal patrol boat beside a disabled sailboat among floating branches. She wears a high-visibility waterproof flotation jacket over a dark operational duty uniform, a fastened buoyancy vest, a radio microphone, weatherproof gloves, a utility belt, and deck boots. Her long dark softly waved hair is secured in a low ponytail, while her visible facial appearance follows the attached portrait only as guidance for a new fictional subject. Braced against the rail, the officer secures a recovery line as a second partially visible crew member transfers one rescued adult in an orange life jacket from the sailboat. A taut line and clipped rescue sling visibly connect the officer's hand, the patrol boat, and the transfer. Broken branches drift around slack rigging; sea spray beads on gear. Documentary maritime-rescue photography, wide three-quarter view, dawn light breaking through rain clouds, with enough body and vessel context to read the uniform, equipment, action, and recovery consequence.
